summary: Michael Aris was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Durham University and the University of London under David L. Snellgrove, later holding positions at St John's College, Wolfson College, St Antony's College, and Harvard University.

Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held an attested post at the Berlin State Library in 1991.

Michael Baxandall studied at Downing College from 1951 to 1954. He held positions at the Victoria and Albert Museum (1961–1965), the Warburg Institute (~1965–1986), Cornell University (~1982–1987), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1986–1996).

Michael Carrithers is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford, in 1977 and served as a Lecturer in Social Anthropology at Durham University from around 1982.

Michael Chase works in the field of philosophy, having studied at the University of Victoria and the École Pratique des Hautes Études. Around 2001, he became a researcher in ancient philosophy at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University (~1983–1987), later holding posts at the University of Sydney and Sri Venkateswara Temple.

Michael Como works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kuo-liang Wang, Carl Bielefeldt, and Bernard Faure, and held an attested post at Columbia University in 2009.

Michael D. Willis is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Victoria and University of Chicago. His career includes posts at the British Museum, De Montfort University, and the European Research Council.
Michael Friedrich is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Friedrich Alexander Bischoff and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1994 to 2021.

Michael G. Morony is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1957–1961) and UCLA (~1961–1971), and served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from around 1974 to 2017.

Michael Hahn specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying at Göttingen, Bonn, and Marburg under Wilhelm Rau and Franz Bernhard. He held posts at Bonn, the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, and the University of Marburg.
Michael Hookham is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at SOAS and the University of London between 1976 and 1984, subsequently serving as Lecturer in Nepali at SOAS from around 1987 to 2021.

Michael J. Sweet worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Richard Hugh Robinson, Ngawang Legden, Khenpo Sangye Tenzin, and Geshe Wangyal, later teaching clinical psychiatry there.
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts degree at San Diego State University under supervisor Sandra A. Wawrytko, attested in 2011.

Michael J. Walsh specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Cape Town (~1985–1989) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1991–1994), where he also conducted doctoral studies under William F. Powell (~1994–2000).

Michael K. Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed undergraduate work at UW–Madison under Harold Scheub. He held faculty posts at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed studies at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter is a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry Moses. He has held positions at Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and Indiana University (attested 2020).
Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1963 to 1967 and later held a post at the University of Oxford.
